title: The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web (Page, Brin, Motwani, Winograd, 1999)
excerpt: Let u be a web page. Then let F_u be the set of pages u points to and B_u be the set of pages that point to u. Let N_u = |F_u| be the number of links from u and let c be a factor used for normalization (so that the total rank of all web pages is constant). We begin by defining a simple ranking, R which is a slightly simplified version of PageRank: R(u) = c Σ_{v∈B_u} R(v)/N_v. This formalizes the intuition that a page has high rank if the sum of the ranks of its backlinks is high. ... Definition: Let E(u) be some vector over the Web pages that corresponds to a source of rank. Then, the PageRank of a set of Web pages is an assignment, R', to the Web pages which satisfies R'(u) = c Σ_{v∈B_u} R'(v)/N_v + cE(u) such that c is maximized and ||R'||_1 = 1. ... The random surfer model: the surfer periodically gets bored and jumps to a random page chosen based on the distribution in E. Computing PageRank: R_0 ← S; loop: R_{i+1} ← A R_i; d ← ||R_i||_1 − ||R_{i+1}||_1; R_{i+1} ← R_{i+1} + dE; δ ← ||R_{i+1} − R_i||_1; while δ > ε.
focus: Explain PageRank as the random-surfer power iteration on a tiny 4-page web graph. Let the learner toggle links between pages and change the damping/teleport probability. Animate the iteration so ranks flow along links until convergence, showing the rank vector and the change delta per iteration. Check that ranks always sum to 1 and that a symmetric graph (e.g. a cycle) gives equal ranks. Explain what happens with a page that has no outgoing links (dangling node) and how the teleport term handles it.
audience: Engineering undergraduate who knows matrices and basic probability.
